decision: took the skill list from Cory House's post and found an upstream for each skill
why: the post names no repos, so each pick is the best-licensed version, not proof of what he runs

decision: kept upstream captures out of git and committed only their provenance
why: several upstreams have no license and some text is Anthropic's
result: public repo carries no unlicensed text

decision: kept council, release-waves, autonomous-delivery and daily-log out; adapt agent-loop-spec and agent-loop-hygiene
why: the rest overlap pstack or need tools a hosted runner lacks

decision: made validation a separate stage with held-out tests the builder never sees
why: the software-factory reports say agents game tests they can edit

decision: land is deterministic code holding the only write token; the factory cannot edit workflows
why: the model must not hold publish rights or loosen its own gates

decision: first unit is a smoke test of model access from a hosted runner
why: riskiest unknown: the proxy lives on a private tailnet

decision: fixed the trust credential subject to GitHub's immutable format
why: token sub is repo:owner@id/repo@id, so the old pattern never matched

decision: added a masked path check after the token exchange passed but the model fetch failed
why: needed to tell DNS, policy and routing apart without leaking tailnet names

decision: switched the runner to a pre-signed ephemeral auth key
why: Tailnet Lock locks out runner devices joined through the trust credential

decision: smoke test passes end to end

why: the auth key expires in 90 days and would otherwise fail silently

decision: accepted the package skeleton after reading the core and rerunning check
why: child summary alone is not proof

decision: widened forbidden paths from .github/workflows to all of .github
why: composite actions and CODEOWNERS steer gates without touching workflow files; the old test called CODEOWNERS ordinary

decision: validate must run the base branch's checks against the candidate
why: a patch could otherwise edit package.json scripts or delete tests to pass

decision: added opt-in human checkpoints before build and before merge, driven by a policy file under .github
why: owner wants a person to see some decisions; the factory must not be able to edit its own checkpoints

decision: accepted the Herdr-on-runner prototype after checking how it decides VERIFIED
why: it asserts on the host's subagent_result message and the child's own session, not on parent text
